profile.reading: This OpenStreetMap record in Alameda County, California, tagged telecom=data_center, carries the name QES Computers. The word "Computers" in a small business name is far more typical of a computer retail, repair, or local IT support shop than of a commercial data center operator, since colocation and hosting businesses almost universally brand around words like data, cloud, or colocation rather than generic "computers" retail language. Public location records tie the coordinates behind this tag to Owens Drive in Pleasanton, a mixed office and retail corridor in the Interstate 580 corridor of Alameda County with numerous business park suites, offices, and street level retail rather than a purpose built data center campus. No address there currently returns a business named QES Computers in available public directories, and no operator website, trade press coverage, or business registration could be located and matched to this name. The overall pattern, a retail sounding name, a mixed use suburban office and retail location, and no independent confirmation of a colocation or hosting business, points toward this being either a defunct small IT retailer once located nearby, a mislabeled point representing an internal server closet rather than a commercial facility, or simply an inaccurate map tag. This entry is filed honestly as unresolved rather than presented as a verified data center.

reading.body:
This entry cannot be evaluated. OpenStreetMap tags it as a data center, but the operator name "QES Computers" follows the branding pattern of computer retail or repair businesses, not commercial data-center operators. Reverse geocoding at the stored coordinates returns a restaurant currently occupying that location. No operator specification page was found because web search quota was exhausted during research.

The record is marked unresolvable. No published power capacity, facility size, or technical specifications are available. No certifications or capabilities can be read from the data.

This facility should not be counted in California's published data-center capacity until an operator specification page confirms its existence, location, and current operation as a data center.
